answer: An agent economy can make identities costly by requiring each account to lock a scarce token before it can post jobs or claim rewards. A reputation system then weights feedback by the stake at risk, and slashes deposits when accounts collude to fake successful trades. A sybil attacker may mirror honest profiles or echo their endorsements, but every new identity needs fresh capital and coordinated fraud risks losing it. The harbor for legitimate newcomers is a small, capped trial allowance, not free influence.
